rule: A local bound directly to a function literal (... local `fun`/`def`/`func`, ... a Kotlin `val f = { }`) is a **named nested function**: ID `outer.f` (Python form), and calls to it are high. Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function ... Anonymous subclass instantiation ...: no constructor edge when the named type is an interface/trait ...; when it is a class (including abstract), `Type#<init>`, constructor
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. `val shout = { .. }` and the local `fun whisper` are named nested functions `com.acme.fn.Worker#run.shout` / `#run.whisper` (Python form `pkg.mod.C#m.inner`); calls inside their bodies have them as caller. The trailing lambda `{ emit(it) }` (line 11), the anonymous Listener member (14) and the anonymous Task member (19) fold into Worker#run. `object : Listener` makes no constructor edge (interface); `object : Task("x")` is Task#<init> (abstract class) on line 17. `l`/`t` are declared Listener/Task; on/exec are body-less declarations of scanned types, high. `f(x)` calls a function-typed parameter: callee `f`, callback, unknown. The for loop's hidden iterator calls are not written calls: no edge.
